title: The Sabbath
lead: The weekly seventh day and its laws: the day on which God rested from creation (Genesis 2:2–3), which Israel was commanded to keep holy (Exodus 20:8–11; Deuteronomy 5:12–15), a sign of the covenant and a gift Jesus called "made for man" (Mark 2:27). For the wider theme of rest in the land, the temple and the rest still to come, see Rest.

sections.b: Genesis 2:2–3 does not use the word Sabbath, but its verb shavat, "stopped," gives the day its name. Israel first keeps it with the manna (Exodus 16:23–30); the Ten Commandments ground it in creation (Exodus 20:11) and in the exodus (Deuteronomy 5:15). It is a sign between God and Israel (Exodus 31:13–17). The prophets call it a delight (Isaiah 58:13–14) and condemn its abuse (Amos 8:5). Jesus heals on the Sabbath and calls himself its Lord (Mark 2:23–3:6). Most Christians worship on Sunday, the day of the resurrection (Acts 20:7; Revelation 1:10); Seventh-day Adventists and Seventh Day Baptists keep Saturday. For Hebrews 4 and the rest still to come, see Rest.
